newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HARD WORK TO RESTORE ASIA/AUSTRALIAN TIES: BANKER
The chairman of a top international bank says Australia needs to work harder to show Asia that the White Australia policy is dead and buried.
Addressing the Committee for Economic Development of Australia, Trevor Rowe from Salomon Brothers says anti-immigration comments by federal MP Pauline Hanson aren't helping business ties with Asia.
Mr Rowe says this country's political and economic future is linked to Asia.
He says he's surprised at how many Asians are having second thoughts about doing business with Australia because of the ongoing race and immigration debate.
GOVT SAYS STATES RESPONSIBLE FOR BLACK DEATHS
The Federal Government says it's doing what it can to help stop Aboriginal deaths in custody, but says responsibility ultimately rests with State and Territory governments.
The continuing rise in the number of such deaths has been highlighted by the Human Rights and Equal Opportunities Commission.
It's accusing the Government of failing to implement the recommendations of the 1989 Aboriginal Deaths in Custody Royal Commission.
Attorney-General Daryl Williams says the government will tackle the issue at its summit on Aboriginal deaths in custody early next year.
ROTHWELLS TWO FOUND GUILTY OF FRAUD
The long running Rothwells conspiracy trial in Perth has ended.
Former director Peter Lucas and independent auditor Louis Carter have been found guilty of fraud.
Both men remain in custody for sentencing on December the 10th.
They were charged with conspiring to conceal the true nature of the Rothwells Merchant Bank's finances before it collapsed in November 1988 with massive debts.
Former Rothwells chief, Laurie Connell was also charged, but died halfway through the trial.
After hearing 14 months of evidence the jury foreman revealed it was not a unanimous verdict, but a majority verdict of ten to two.
MIGRANT BENEFIT CHANGES BLOCKED
Federal Shadow Attorney-General, Nick Bolkus, says the Senate has forced the Government to keep its election promise by blocking moves to change benefit requirements for migrants.

The Government had proposed to make newly arrived migrants wait two years before they were eligible for a range of benefits, including the maternity allowance, carer's pension, health care cards and parenting benefits.
Senator Bolkus says the Coalition never indicated during the federal election campaign that it was intending to extend the waiting period for such benefits.
He says to do so now would be dishonest.
The waiting period for a number of unemployment payments and student and youth assistance has already been extended to two years.
MURDER-SUICIDE ON GOLD COAST

An 11-year-old girl witnessed the murder suicide of her parents on Queensland's Gold Coast last night and called police. Gold Coast CIB Detective Senior Sergeant John Pointing says police and ambulance officers were quickly on the scene.
He says 37-year old Lee Anthony Worboys was found hanged, while his wife Christine Kay Worboys had head injuries and died in hospital several hours later.
Senior Sergeant Pointing says a domestic dispute is believed to have led to the man killing his wife and then himself.
VISITORS TO PNG WARNED ABOUT CURFEW
The Foreign Affairs Department has warned Australians planning to visit Papua New Guinea about the curfew imposed by the PNG Government.
The curfew operates from 10pm until 4am each day in areas including the Capital district, Central Province, Lae City and Mount Hagen.
The Department has warned all Australians travelling to PNG to exercise due care and maintain a very high level of security.
It also warns that anyone planning to visit Bougainville Province should only do so with the authorisation of the P-N-G Government.
GOLD COAST MURDER TRIAL CONTINUES
A Gold Coast court has heard that an 18 year-old youth doused a vagrant with metho and set him alight because he'd tried to molest his 14 year-old friend.
The two youths, who can't be named are facing murder charges following the death of 54 year old Noel Richards.
Mr Richards was found unconscious late last month with burns to 50 percent of his body...he died several weeks later.
In Commital procedings today a witness told the court the 18 year old told her he and his friend had been talking to the homeless man near a pool.
She alleged the defendent told her he went to the toilet and when he came back the other youth told him the old man tried to molest him.
She says defendent told her he then threw metho on the man, and lit him up.
The hearing is continuing.
CRICKET: BLEWETT, MCINTYRE IN FOR AUSSIES
The Australian Cricket selectors have named a thirteen strong squad for the second test against the West Indies starting in Sydney on Friday.
South Australian Greg Blewett has been brought in to replace the injured Steve Waugh with state team-mate leg-spinner Peter McIntyre also included.
The final twelve will be announced following Thursday's training.
The rest of the squad is Taylor captain, Healy, Elliott, Ponting, Bevan, McGrath, Gillespie, Kasprowicz, Warne, Reiffel and Mark Waugh.
